definitions.gloss: to talk back; to retort; to answer back
definitions.explanation: To respond defiantly or argumentatively to something someone has said. Implies pushing back against criticism, a scolding, or an accusation.

examples.japanese: {親|おや}に{言|い}い{返|かえ}してはいけない。
examples.english: You must not talk back to your parents.

examples.japanese: {悔|くや}しかったが、{何|なに}も{言|い}い{返|かえ}せなかった。
examples.english: I was frustrated, but I couldn't say anything back.

examples.japanese: {上司|じょうし}に{理不尽|りふじん}なことを{言|い}われたので、つい{言|い}い{返|かえ}してしまった。
examples.english: My boss said something unreasonable, so I couldn't help talking back.

notes:
USAGE:
{言|い}い{返|かえ}す implies defiance or resistance. It is different from simply replying ({返事|へんじ}する). Often appears in negative contexts: either someone is being told not to talk back, or they wish they could have but didn't.

COMMON PATTERNS:
Godan verb (consonant stem: {返|かえ}す). Transitive.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {言|い}い{返|かえ}せない (unable to retort)
- {言|い}い{返|かえ}す{言葉|ことば}もない (to be speechless / have no comeback)
- つい{言|い}い{返|かえ}してしまう (to end up talking back despite oneself)

FORMS:
{言|い}う (to say) + {返|かえ}す (to return). The compound means "to say something back."
